evals.prompt: /explore "a way for small dental practices to chase unpaid invoices"
expectations: brief has the twelve headings in template order
## Success signal holds exactly one line
frontmatter keys are the seven of §5 in order

evals.prompt: /explore "an app that tells you which houseplant is dying" then the user answers Kill
/explore "shift swapping for restaurant staff" then the user answers Park and picks the 90-day option
expectations: revisit_on parses as YYYY-MM-DD and is later than decided_on
the brief is still on disk

evals.prompt: /explore "invoice chasing for dental practices" then the user answers Promote
expectations: carry_forward holds exactly seven entries in the order given in the template
consumer values are the four skill names of the carry-forward table

evals.prompt: /explore IDEA-001 --remedy FLOW-002,FLOW-004 with a prior brief and a Discover report on disk
evals.expected_output: a brief whose FLOW-002 and FLOW-004 rows changed and whose other rows did not
expectations: FLOW-001 and FLOW-003 rows are byte-identical to the prior brief

evals.prompt: /explore IDEA-001 --remedy FLOW-002,FLOW-009 where FLOW-009 is absent from the brief
evals.expected_output: a brief with an open_questions entry naming FLOW-009
expectations: open_questions holds a line containing FLOW-009
the FLOW-002 row differs from the prior brief
## Core flows still holds 3 to 5 rows
no row with id FLOW-009 was invented

evals.prompt: /explore "a budgeting tool for freelancers" where state.toml shows [explore].started_at six days ago
evals.expected_output: a brief at status: mocked and no decision.yaml
expectations: the run reached step 9 and asked the decision question
the three option labels are Kill, Park, Promote

evals.prompt: /explore "a tool for tracking what a book club has read"
expectations: the file carries the seven §5 top-level keys and mode: "sketch"
flows[] holds one object per ## Core flows row with the same FLOW-nnn ids in the same order
constraints holds the four fixed keys with no_backend, no_auth and no_persistence true
